title: Telemetry honeypot and decisioning layer to reduce noisy burn-rate pages
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight 'telemetry honeypot' ingestion path and a decisioning layer that fuses tracing hooks, metric/log artifacts, and probe results to suppress false-positive burn-rate alerts and produce contextual pager signals. The goal is to reduce noisy pages for oncall while preserving high-fidelity detection for real SLO degradation. Deliverables: honeypot instrumentation, decision engine (heuristics + anomaly model), integration with pager policy and runbooks, and dashboards for verification.
background: Our paging data for the last two quarters shows ~28% of burn-rate pages resolved without any correlated error traces or user-facing degradation. Noise is costly for SREs and product teams. Existing mitigation (static burn-rate white-lists and manual suppression windows) is brittle and leads to either missed incidents or unnecessary pages. We need a systematic way to: 1) surface signal gaps (missing traces/metrics) and 2) make a conservative suppression decision when telemetry indicates a low-likelihood customer impact event.
success_criteria: 1) Reduce actionable burn-rate pages by >=30% in two months on pilot services. 2) False negative rate for major degradations <2% (tracked via retrospective sampling). 3) New dashboards show correlated telemetry coverage and suppression decisions for each alert.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement honeypot ingestion stream (sampled traffic that tags requests as honeypot) and minimal trace hook to collect path/model/sequence-length context. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Build decisioning layer that: a) checks for correlated error traces/log spikes, b) runs lightweight anomaly model on metric windows, c) applies conservative suppression rule-set with TTLs and manual override. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Integrate with pager policies (PagerDuty/Grafana alerts) and add canary rollout for two backend services. Phase 4: Observability dashboards and runbook updates.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Suppression risk: overly aggressive suppression could hide real degradations; mitigated by conservative heuristics, short TTLs, and automatic escalation to synthetic probes.
- Latency vs telemetry coverage: richer trace hooks add overhead; we will limit to 0.5% sampling for production and full sampling in honeypot.
- Privacy/compliance: honeypot traces must scrub PII; coordinated with security to ensure KMS and audit logs are enabled.
work_notes: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with SRE, Observability, and Product. Agreed on target pilot services (text-generation-api and embeddings-pipeline).
2026-02-25: Prototype honeypot header implemented in runtime sidecar. Sidecar tags 1% of traffic as HOOK=true for full trace capture. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/412)

2026-03-02: Decisioning design reviewed with PM and SRE. Chosen approach: deterministic heuristic gate + lightweight isolation-based anomaly score (moving-median + MAD) for speed. Feedback: add synthetic-probe fallback before suppressing pages. (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Honeypot+Design)
2026-03-06: Security review stubbed: confirmed no secrets in honeypot traces; PII scrubbing library integration required. Assigned to Camille Ng. (ticket: ENG-883455)

2026-03-08: Implemented initial decision rule: if burn-rate triggered AND honeypot shows no error traces for same request-path AND anomaly score < 3 sigma AND synthetic-probe healthy, then mark as suppressed with automagic annotation and create a low-priority audit incident. Tuned TTL to 5m.
2026-03-09: Integration test run on staging created suppressed alerts correctly but exposed a race where synthetic-probe latency was >10s on cold starts; added probe warmup and cache priming in plan.
2026-03-10: Preparing canary rollout for text-generation-api (10% of traffic) on 2026-03-15. Dashboard templates in Grafana created (link below).
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee) 2026-03-03: Emphasize audit trail and ability to force-open suppressed alerts for postmortem. Add a 'preview' mode to see what would have been suppressed.

SRE (Priya Menon) 2026-03-04: Keep suppression logic readable and reversible; prefer rule config in YAML in repo rather than single hard-coded service. Ensure alert tags include suppression_reason and telemetry_ids.
Design (Camille Ng) 2026-03-06: Dashboard must clearly show coverage delta (traces vs metrics vs logs) so teams can fix instrumentation gaps instead of relying on suppression.
Security (Dmitri Volk) 2026-03-06: Require scrubbing and retention TTL of honeypot traces to 7 days max for pilot.
